newsitem.title: INDIA: Buying by state firms lifts Indian cotton prices.
newsitem.headline: Buying by state firms lifts Indian cotton prices.

text.p: Indian cotton prices gained on Wednesday as a result of increased buying by state-owned agencies including the Cotton Corporation of India, dealers said.
A planned strike on Thursday, when all markets will close to protest a tax hike and other charges by the government, prompted state firms to buy more cotton.
In the spot deals Bengal-deshi rose by five rupees to 825/855 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned climbed up by 10 rupees to 1,410/1,650 rupees.
F-414 gained by 10/15 rupees to 1,840/1,855 rupees. Gujarat Sankar-4 (long-staple) was steady on thin volumes.
